name: Tualatin
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Tualatin, OR 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Tualatin, OR: the Tualatin Light Parades with Santa on three December nights and Santa Day at Red Sled Market.
lede: Tualatin celebrates Christmas on wheels and by the lake: three neighborhood Light Parades with Santa in the lead car, a long-running tree lighting at Tualatin Commons and a family holiday market on Nyberg Road.
celebrates: The City of Tualatin Parks and Recreation department runs the Tualatin Light Parades, three evenings when decorated cars drive 5 to 6 miles through a different part of town, led by Tualatin Police with Santa in the first vehicle. Families watch from front yards, streets and parks, and the city posts maps and a live tracker. Residents can enter their own cars for free. Tualatin Commons, around the lake on SW Nyberg Street, has long hosted the city's tree lighting with youth choirs. Red Sled Market, a craft market on SW Nyberg Road, adds Santa photos and kids' crafts.
lastyear: In 2025 the Tualatin Light Parades were planned over three nights, December 5 to 7, and the City of Tualatin invited residents to decorate their own vehicles and join one, two or all three. The city's parade page also shows photos from earlier years, including 2020, 2021, 2023 and 2024, so families can see what the lit-up cars look like. Planning for the 2026 season brought new routes, which the city announced in November.
facts: Tualatin's Holiday Lights Parade began in December 2020, when the pandemic cancelled the usual tree lighting. The first three parades were on Saturday nights, and the city gave out free LED car-lighting kits paid for with federal CARES Act funds. The city's older tree lighting, Starry Nights and Holiday Lights, floated a Christmas tree in the center of Tualatin Commons lake, with model boats decked in lights, and Santa arrived escorted by police officers dressed as elves. Red Sled Market is celebrating 30 years in 2026.
trains: Tualatin has its own WES Commuter Rail station at 18955 SW Boones Ferry Road. WES is TriMet's weekday commuter train between Beaverton, Tigard, Tualatin and Wilsonville, running at rush hour only, so it suits a school-day ride more than a weekend outing. For Christmas trains, head to nearby Lake Oswego, where the Willamette Shore Trolley runs vintage trips along the river. In Portland, the Oregon Rail Heritage Center runs the Holiday Express steam train, and the Washington Park and Zoo Railway runs at the Oregon Zoo.

faq: What are the Tualatin Light Parades?

They are a City of Tualatin Parks and Recreation tradition. Decorated cars drive 5 to 6 miles through Tualatin neighborhoods on three evenings, led by Tualatin Police with Santa in the lead vehicle. You can watch from your own street or a park along the route, and the city posts maps and a live tracker.
Can our family be in the Tualatin Light Parades?

Yes. Registration is only required for vehicles, it is free and it is limited for each parade. Residents may sign up for any or all of the parades. Decorations should use LED lights, stay secure in wind and rain, and be family friendly. Everyone must stay inside the vehicle, and nothing may be thrown from it.
How did the Tualatin Light Parades start?

The city began them in December 2020, after the pandemic cancelled its tree lighting. Residents decorated their own cars and drove set routes on three Saturday nights, accompanied by the mayor, police motorcycles and a fire engine. The parades were so popular that they became an annual tradition.
Where is the Tualatin Commons tree lighting?

Tualatin Commons is the lakeside area around SW Nyberg Street at 8325 SW Nyberg Street. Past Starry Nights and Holiday Lights events lit a Christmas tree afloat in the lake, with youth choirs, hot cocoa and cookies, and Santa arriving at the end of the countdown.
Where can kids see Santa in Tualatin?

Red Sled Market, at 7111 SW Nyberg Road, holds a Santa Day with free photos, kids' crafts, hot cocoa and candy canes. Santa also leads the Tualatin Light Parades in the first car. Check the market's events page for the day and hours before you go.
Is there a train near Tualatin for kids?

Yes. WES Commuter Rail stops in Tualatin on weekdays at rush hour. The Willamette Shore Trolley runs vintage trips from nearby Lake Oswego, and Portland's Oregon Rail Heritage Center runs the Holiday Express steam train in December. Check each operator for current dates and tickets.
